subject: Editing irregular strings in large climate dataset...

messages.author: 4dee24c578d7691c
messages.subject: Editing irregular strings in large climate dataset...
parts:
Hello wonderful Davis R Community,

Yet again, I'm consulting this great community of helpful R experts to
see if someone has any ideas on how to read in, and edit, files with
irregular combinations of letters and numbers. These data are from the
US National Historical Climatology Network. These data are in rows by
year. The first column is the station ID, subsequent rows refer to
monthly precipitation data followed by total precip with multiple
quality control notes and flags. I included the metadata as a text file
(data_format.txt) so you can see what the numbers and letters refer to.
An example of the data is attached as well.

Unfortunately when I read in the dataset with readLines I end up with a
number of issues such as uneven number of columns and letters and
punctuation marks (which are QC flags) remaining pasted on to the
numbers rather than separated into columns.

Has anyone encountered a similar datset - and perhaps have some
suggestions on efficient processing? Favorite functions or packages? I
have tried a number of approaches - like replacing the letters with
spaces and letters - but I can't quite seem to create a dataset with the
data in the correct columns.

Thanks - in advance!!!,
Stella

--
Stella Copeland
Post-doctoral Researcher
Harrison Lab, Plant Ecology
UC Davis

messages.author: 2226e6c311219eb7
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Editing irregular strings in large climate dataset...
parts:
Hi Stella

I don't have time to check it, but something like

d = read.fwf( "weather.example.txt", c(11, 4, 5, 1, 1, 1, 5, rep(1, 125-32+1), 5, 1, 1, 1))

should do the basics. From the documentation, it seems to be a fixed width format, hence the read.fwf().

You can specify the colClasses to specify which are characters, which are integers, etc.
cols = rep("character", 105)
cols[c(2, 3, 7, 102)] = "integer"
and then
d = read.fwf( "weather.example.txt", c(11, 4, 5, 1, 1, 1, 5, rep(1, 125-32+1), 5, 1, 1, 1), colClasses = cols)

and similarly put the column names on with the col.names parameter.

My column widths are probably off by one in several places!

D.
